name: Plank Pose
intro:
Plank Pose (Phalakasana) is a powerful core-strengthening yoga posture that builds stability, endurance, and full-body strength. In this pose, the body forms a straight line from head to heels, resembling a strong, steady plank. It engages multiple muscle groups simultaneously, including the core, arms, shoulders, back, and legs.

Phalakasana is commonly used as a transitional pose in yoga sequences, especially in Sun Salutations. Despite appearing simple, it requires proper alignment and muscle engagement to perform effectively. Holding this pose strengthens the abdominal muscles, improves posture, and enhances overall balance and coordination.

Regular practice of Plank Pose helps develop mental focus and resilience, as it challenges both the body and mind. It is particularly beneficial for building core strength, which supports the spine and reduces the risk of injuries. With consistent practice, it improves stamina, stability, and overall body control.

steps.text: Start in a tabletop position with your hands under your shoulders.
Step your feet back one at a time, extending your legs straight.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core, thighs, and glutes.
Press your palms firmly into the ground and keep your arms straight.
Keep your neck neutral and gaze slightly down.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.

benefits: Strengthens core muscles including abs and lower back
Builds strength in arms, shoulders, and wrists
Helps in toning the entire body
Reduces risk of back injuries by strengthening core
avoid: You have wrist injuries or severe wrist pain
You have severe lower back pain
You are recovering from abdominal surgery
You feel excessive strain or discomfort while holding the pose
You have high blood pressure (consult a doctor before practice)
